title: 38-54_Grievance of United Academics
text:
VERMONT LABOR RELATIONS BOARD
GRIEVANCE OF )
UNITED ACADEMICS ) Docket No. 25-05
DECISION AND ORDER ON MOTION TO DISMISS
Introduction
On 1/16/25, United Academics (“Union”) filed a Grievance with the Vermont Labor
Relations Board (“Board”) alleging the University of Vermont, (“UVM” “University”), violated
Articles 16.1 and 16.2 of the of the parties’ Collective Bargaining Agreement (“CBA”) and past
practice associated with these articles when it unilaterally imposed the “Course Equivalencies
Guidelines” (“Guidelines”) on the College of Education and Social Services. Articles 16.1 and
16.2 of the CBA govern faculty workloads. Article 16.1 contains the following provision.
“Unless the faculty member is told otherwise by July 1 for 12 month faculty and by June 1 for all
other faculty, the workload plan developed by the faculty member and Chair for the Submission
to the Dean shall be considered approved by the Dean.”
The University has filed with the Board a motion to dismiss asserting the Union failed to
file a timely Grievance with the University because it was filed more than thirty days after the
challenged Guidelines went into effect, and the Union failed to allege an injury to a member and
the Board lacks jurisdiction to hear the Grievance.
Background
The CBA outlines the process for distributing approved course equivalency guidelines.
“Upon approval by the Dean and Provost, these course equivalency guidelines shall be
distributed to faculty and posted electronically, and also sent to the Union, and will be
implemented in the immediately subsequent academic year.” Article 16.15. The Office of the
54

Provost approved the Guidelines on March 22, 2022, and they were posted online and distributed
to the Union.
The Union filed its Grievance with the University on October 8, 2024.
DECISION
The Employer has filed a motion to dismiss claiming the grievance was not timely filed
with UVM and the Union failed to allege an actual harm or injury, and therefore, the Board lacks
jurisdiction to hear the grievance.
The Vermont Labor Relations Board seeks to resolve an issue on the merits, unless the
Board Rules of Practice or the Collective Bargaining Agreement require it to be dismissed on
procedural grounds. See Grievance of Adam Mickel, 33 VLRB 282, (2016) (citing Grievance of
Monti, 10 VLRB 246 (1987)). Where the collective bargaining agreement between the parties
sets out specific times for filing grievances at earlier steps in the grievance process, or before the
Board, and the grievance did not adhere to the timelines outlined in the CBA, the Board has
refused to consider the Grievance. See Grievance of Benoit, 31 VLRB 237, 249-50 (2011);
Grievance of Ulrich, 12 VLRB 230, 239 (1989), aff’d, 157 Vt. 290 (1981). The CBA provides a
means to resolve conflicts early in the process. See Grievance of Mason, 16 VLRB 222, 237
(1993). See also In re Bushey, 142 Vt. 290, 294 (1982). Failure to adhere to these timelines
impedes this goal of early resolution. See Mason 16 VLRB at 237.
Article 12.8 of the CBA states that “a formal grievance must be filed at the appropriate
step within thirty (30) days following the time at which the faculty member and/or the Union
were or reasonably should have been aware of the existence of the situation that is the basis for
the grievance.” The Union filed the Grievance with UVM on October 8, 2024. The Union
alleges the Guidelines impose the condition that workloads can be changed up to the Add/Drop
55

period. The Union claims the Guidelines violate the CBA and past practice because it extends
beyond July 1 the determination of the workload plan. The Union asserts the Guidelines negate
the predictability of the protections of Articles 16.1 and 2 and allow the University unfettered
authority to reduce faculty members’ FTE after the Add/Drop period, long after the July 1
deadline imposed by the CBA. The risk of reducing the FTE, the Union claims, can potentially
impact the financial and benefit status of faculty members.
The Guidelines were issued on March 22, 2022. The Guidelines provide the following:
CHAIR DISCRETION: The guidelines below are meant to aid chairs from all
departments in determining equivalencies for large classes. Final determinations will be
specified through the workload process.
. . . .
*Note that all courses are assigned a 1 Course equivalency on the workload and then if
the course is overenrolled, the instructor receives and additional “banked” credit to be
used within two years. The only exception is courses that are traditionally overenrolled,
or have been overenrolled within the last two years. If the aforementioned courses do not
meet the enrollment numbers required to meet the credit articulated in the workload, then
the workload shall be revised to reflect the actual course equivalency.
1. A 0.25-Course equivalency credit will be provided in the workload for 3-credit courses
with enrollments of 31-50 at the completion of the Add/Drop period.
2. A 0.5-Course equivalency credit will be provided in the workload for 3-credit courses
with enrollments of 51-74 at the completion of the Add/Drop period. Faculty can also
request 10 hours per week of TA support. Rejection of TA support will not lead to an
increase in course equivalency.
3. A 0.75-Course equivalency credit will be provided in the workload for 3-credit courses
with enrollments of 75 -99 at the completion of the Add/Drop period. Faculty can also
request 10 hours per week of TA support. Rejection of TA support will not lead to an
increase in course equivalency.
4. A 1-Course equivalency credit will be provided in the workload for 3-credit courses
with enrollments of 100-150 at the completion of the Add/Drop period. Faculty can also
request 20 hours per week of TA support. Rejection of TA support will not lead to an
increase in course equivalency.
5. A 1.5-Course equivalency credit will be provided in the workload for 3-credit courses
with enrollments of 151-200 at the completion of the Add/Drop period. Faculty can also
request 30 hours per week of TA support. Rejection of TA support will not lead to [sic]
increase in course equivalency.
56

6. A 2-Course equivalency credit will be provided in the workload for 3-credit courses
with enrollments at 201-299 at the completion of the Add/Drop period. Faculty can also
request 30 hours per week of TA support. Rejection of TA support will not lead to an
increase in course equivalency.
Grievance Exhibit 2, College of Education and Social Services (CESS) Course
Equivalencies Guidelines, Revised March 9, 2022.
Faculty contributed to the development and editing of the Guidelines. “Faculty in all
Departments provided input into the document’s revisions via written comments and discussions
held during formal and informal meetings held in October and November of 2021, and
January/February 2022.” Id. at Notes.
The risk of harm the Union has identified in its Grievance, the loss of financial
predictability to faculty, was known to faculty when it participated in the development of the
Guidelines, and when they were published in March 2022. The Guidelines outline the change in
course equivalency credits that will be determined “at the completion of the Add/Drop period.”
Exhibit 2. The Union has not identified a new harm that could only be discovered by the passage
of time, nor has it outlined why it was unable to reasonably be aware of this harm back in 2022.
The Union has asserted the same harm or injury that existed back on March 22, 2022.
“Reducing a faculty member’s FTE after the add/drop period has the potential to seriously
impact the financial and benefit status of the faculty member and their family members.”
Grievance Statement at 5.
Faculty were aware, or reasonably should have been aware, of the existence of the risk of
harm which they assert in the Grievance when the Guidelines were issued in March 2022. The
publication of the Guidelines on March 22, 2022, disclosed the potential or risk that course
equivalencies could change and be impacted by the actual enrollments determined at the
57

completion of the Add/Drop period. The time to file the Grievance was back in 2022, within
thirty days of when the Union or Faculty or both were made aware or reasonably should have
been aware of this situation.
Grievant did not file its initial Grievance within thirty (30) days as required under the
CBA. The Board will apply the terms to which the parties have agreed and will not alter the
deadline.
The Board does not need to decide whether the Union has alleged an actual injury in fact,
because the Board has concluded the Union failed to file a timely Grievance with the University
by filing its Grievance of the Guidelines, issued by the Provost in March 2022, on October 8,
2024, well beyond the requisite thirty (30) days required by the CBA.
58

ORDER
For the reasons stated above, the motion to dismiss filed by the University is GRANTED.
Dated this 15th day of July 2025, at Montpelier, Vermont.
VERMONT LABOR RELATIONS BOARD
